claims.text: About 90% of anogenital warts caused by HPV 6 or 11, nononcogenic types
claims.quote: Anogenital warts are a common disease, and 90% are caused by nononcogenic HPV types 6 or 11.

claims.text: Types 16, 18, 31, 33, 35 only occasionally found in warts
claims.quote: HPV types 16, 18, 31, 33, and 35 also are occasionally identified in anogenital warts

claims.text: No definitive evidence that any one recommended treatment is superior
claims.quote: No definitive evidence indicates that any one recommended treatment is superior to another

claims.text: Treatment choice guided by size, number, site, preference, cost, convenience, adverse effects, provider experience
claims.quote: Treatment of anogenital warts should be guided by wart size, number, and anatomic site; patient preference; ... cost of treatment; convenience; adverse effects; and provider experience.

claims.text: Imiquimod 5% at bedtime 3 times a week up to 16 weeks
claims.quote: Imiquimod 5% cream should be applied once at bedtime, 3 times/week for up to 16 weeks

claims.text: Imiquimod 3.75% once at bedtime nightly up to 8 weeks
claims.quote: Similarly, imiquimod 3.75% cream should be applied once at bedtime every night for up to 8 weeks

claims.text: Imiquimod: immune enhancer stimulating interferon and cytokines
claims.quote: topically active immune enhancer that stimulates production of interferon and other cytokines.

claims.text: Podofilox antimitotic causing wart necrosis
claims.quote: Podofilox (podophyllotoxin) is a patient-applied antimitotic drug that causes wart necrosis.

claims.text: Podofilox twice a day for 3 days, then 4 days off
claims.quote: should be applied to anogenital warts 2 times/day for 3 days, followed by 4 days of no therapy

claims.text: Podofilox area max 10 cm2 and 0.5 mL per day
claims.quote: The total wart area treated should not exceed 10 cm2, and the total volume of podofilox should be limited to 0.5 mL/day.

claims.text: Sinecatechins: green tea extract, active product catechins
claims.quote: Sinecatechins is a patient-applied, green-tea extract with an active product (catechins).

claims.text: Sinecatechins three times a day, 0.5 cm strand per wart
claims.quote: Sinecatechins 15% ointment should be applied 3 times/day (0.5-cm strand of ointment to each wart)

claims.text: Avoid sexual contact while sinecatechins on skin
claims.quote: Genital, anal, and oral sexual contact should be avoided while the ointment is on the skin.

claims.text: Sinecatechins not recommended in HIV, other immunocompromise, genital herpes
claims.quote: This medication is not recommended for persons with HIV infection, other immunocompromised conditions, or genital herpes

claims.text: Imiquimod may weaken condoms and diaphragms (CDC)
claims.quote: Might weaken condoms and vaginal diaphragms.

claims.text: Cryotherapy destroys warts by thermal-induced cytolysis
claims.quote: Cryotherapy is a provider-administered therapy that destroys warts by thermal-induced cytolysis.

claims.text: Pain, necrosis, sometimes blistering with cryotherapy
claims.quote: Pain during and after application of the liquid nitrogen, followed by necrosis and sometimes blistering, is common.

claims.text: TCA/BCA 80-90% destroy warts by chemical coagulation of proteins; repeat weekly if necessary
claims.quote: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) or bichloroacetic acid (BCA) 80%–90% solution ... destroy warts by chemical coagulation of proteins. ... TCA or BCA treatment can be repeated weekly if necessary.

claims.text: Apply small amount, let dry; can spread and damage adjacent tissue
claims.quote: A small amount should be applied only to the warts and allowed to dry ... can spread rapidly and damage adjacent tissues if applied excessively.

claims.text: Surgical removal methods; majority of warts at a single visit, recurrence can occur
claims.quote: Surgical removal by tangential scissor excision, tangential shave excision, curettage, laser, or electrosurgery ... Surgical therapy has the advantage of eliminating the majority of warts at a single visit, although recurrence can occur.

claims.text: Pigment changes with ablative modalities
claims.quote: Persistent hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation can occur with ablative modalities

claims.text: Alternative regimens with fewer data; podophyllin resin no longer recommended
claims.quote: Podophyllin resin is no longer a recommended regimen because of the number of safer regimens available ... which include podophyllin resin, intralesional interferon, photodynamic therapy, and topical cidofovir.

claims.text: Site-specific regimens: urethral meatus (cryotherapy, surgical removal); vaginal, cervical and intra-anal (cryotherapy, surgical removal, TCA/BCA); external sites list
claims.quote: Recommended Regimens for Urethral Meatus Warts: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen; Surgical removal. Recommended Regimens for Intra-Anal Warts: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, Surgical removal, Trichloracetic acid (TCA) or Bichloroacetic acid (BCA) 80%–90% solution.

claims.text: No cryoprobe in vagina
claims.quote: The use of a cryoprobe in the vagina is not recommended because of the risk for vaginal perforation and fistula formation.

claims.text: Cervical warts: specialist consult, biopsy exophytic warts before treatment
claims.quote: Management of cervical warts should include consultation with a specialist. ... a biopsy evaluation to exclude HSIL should be performed before treatment is initiated.

claims.text: Intra-anal: colorectal specialist; seen mostly after receptive anal intercourse
claims.quote: Management of intra-anal warts should include consultation with a colorectal specialist. ... Intra-anal warts are observed predominantly in persons who have had receptive anal intercourse

claims.text: HIV/immunosuppression: same treatment; larger/more numerous, respond less, recur more
claims.quote: such persons can have larger or more numerous lesions ... might not respond to therapy as well ... might have more frequent recurrences ... data do not support altered approaches to treatment for persons with HIV infection.

claims.text: SCC can resemble warts in immunosuppressed; biopsy suspicious lesions
claims.quote: Squamous cell carcinomas arising in or resembling anogenital warts might occur more frequently ... requiring biopsy for confirmation of diagnosis for suspicious cases

claims.text: Diagnosis usually by visual inspection; HPV testing not recommended for diagnosis
claims.quote: Diagnosis of anogenital warts is usually made by visual inspection ... HPV testing is not recommended for anogenital wart diagnosis

claims.text: Biopsy indications: atypical lesions; uncertain diagnosis, no response, worsening
claims.quote: which is indicated if lesions are atypical (e.g., pigmented, indurated, affixed to underlying tissue ... the diagnosis is uncertain, the lesions do not respond to standard therapy, or the disease worsens during therapy

claims.text: Some lesions resemble warts; condyloma lata of secondary syphilis diagnosed serologically
claims.quote: Some anogenital lesions can resemble anogenital warts (condyloma accuminata) ... Condyloma lata, a manifestation of secondary syphilis, can be diagnosed by serologic tests

claims.text: Benefit from testing for other STIs
claims.quote: Because genital warts can be sexually transmitted, persons with genital warts benefit from testing for other STIs.

claims.text: Usually painless; can be painful or itchy by size and location; common site vaginal introitus
claims.quote: Anogenital warts are usually asymptomatic ... depending on the size and anatomic location, they can be painful or pruritic ... including around the vaginal introitus

claims.text: Transmission without visible warts; partners share HPV
claims.quote: can be passed on to another person, even without visible signs of warts. ... Sex partners tend to share HPV, even though signs of HPV (e.g., warts) might occur in only one or neither partner.

claims.text: Condoms might lower chance; HPV can infect areas not covered
claims.quote: Condoms might lower the chances of transmitting genital warts if used consistently and correctly ... HPV can infect areas that are not covered by a condom and might not fully protect against HPV.

claims.text: Warts can develop months or years after acquiring HPV; time of acquisition cannot be determined
claims.quote: Genital warts can develop months or years after acquiring HPV. ... Time of HPV acquisition cannot be definitively determined.

claims.text: Wart HPV types differ from cancer types; no more frequent Pap tests
claims.quote: The types of HPV that cause genital warts are different from the types that can cause cancer. ... Women with genital warts do not need Pap tests more often than other women.

claims.text: Therapies might reduce but probably do not eradicate HPV; warts often recur esp first 3 months; HPV may persist after warts gone
claims.quote: Available therapies for anogenital warts might reduce, but probably do not eradicate, HPV infectivity. ... genital warts often recur after treatment, especially during the first 3 months.

claims.text: Untreated warts may resolve, stay, or grow
claims.quote: If left untreated, anogenital warts can resolve spontaneously, remain unchanged, or increase in size or number.

claims.text: Warts respond within 3 months; change treatment if no substantial improvement
claims.quote: Anogenital warts typically respond within 3 months of therapy. ... A new treatment modality should be selected when no substantial improvement is observed

claims.text: Inform current partners; HPV testing of partners not recommended; partners may benefit from exam and STI tests; no recommendation on future partners
claims.quote: Persons should inform current partners about having genital warts. ... HPV testing of sex partners of persons with genital warts is not recommended ... Partners might benefit from a physical examination to detect genital warts and tests for other STIs.

claims.text: Pregnancy: podofilox and sinecatechins not used; imiquimod low risk but avoid
claims.quote: Podofilox, podophyllin, and sinecatechins should not be used during pregnancy. Imiquimod appears to pose low risk but should be avoided until more data are available.

claims.text: Pregnancy: warts proliferate/friable; removal can be considered; resolution may be incomplete
claims.quote: Anogenital warts can proliferate and become friable during pregnancy. ... Although removal of warts during pregnancy can be considered ... resolution might be incomplete or poor until pregnancy is complete

claims.text: Cesarean not solely to prevent transmission; indicated if outlet obstructed or excessive bleeding
claims.quote: cesarean delivery should not be performed solely to prevent transmission of HPV infection to the newborn. ... Cesarean delivery is indicated ... if the pelvic outlet is obstructed ... if vaginal delivery would result in excessive bleeding.

claims.text: Respiratory papillomatosis rare; route not understood; counsel about low risk
claims.quote: Rarely, HPV types 6 and 11 can cause respiratory papillomatosis among infants and children ... the route of transmission (i.e., transplacental, perinatal, or postnatal) is not completely understood.

claims.text: CDC current treatment recommendations are the 2021 guidelines
claims.quote: Last Reviewed: July 22, 2021.

references.cited_as: Workowski KA, Bachmann LH, Chan PA, et al. Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(4):1-187. Anogenital warts section, CDC web page last reviewed July 22, 2021. Accessed November 7, 2026.

claims.text: 51% clearance imiquimod 2% or 5% vs 6% placebo, HIV-negative, NNT 2.2
claims.quote: In five trials with HIV-negative patients complete clearance of warts at the end of treatment occurred in 51% of patients treated with imiquimod 2% or 5% cream and 6% of placebo treated patients. The number needed to treat was 2.2

claims.text: Not effective in one trial in HIV-positive patients
claims.quote: Imiquimod was not effective in one trial in HIV-positive patients.

claims.text: Clearance plus no recurrence 37% vs 4%
claims.quote: In three trials complete clearance of warts at the end of treatment plus no recurrence occurred in 37% of patients treated with imiquimod 5% cream and 4% of those treated with placebo.

references.cited_as: Moore RA, Edwards JE, Hopwood J, Hicks D. Imiquimod for the treatment of genital warts: a quantitative systematic review. BMC Infect Dis. 2001;1:3.
